# 5. Interaction Flow ## 5.1. Complaint Handling Overall Flow The Complaint Handling Agent leverages DPI (Deep Packet Inspection) and single-domain reported data to automatically analyze subscriber complaint issues. It correlates them with known/common issues, non-network-related problems, and network-related problems for automated handling.Upon demarcation of network problems, it collaborates with single-domain fault Agents or network optimization Agents to perform root cause localization of the complaint issue. The system then provides handling recommendations, enables automated closed-loop resolution, and delivers closed-loop verification capabilities. The agent-based diagnosis mode and Copilot H5 plug-in/LPI integration mode are used. [Figure: Complaint handling overall flow] Step 1: represent the complaint occurrence phase. In the above example, the service layer cross-domain identifies the complaint as a wireless single-domain issue. It then sends diagnostic information to the corresponding resource. Then, repair suggestions sent by the resource layer agent and determines that automatic repair is not possible, prompting the initiation of an onsite ticket. Steps 7-8 represent the execution and handling phase of complaint . In the above example, the cross-domain agent receives receive the base station aging root cause and feed back into the Ticket system, then the Ticket System create a task to request onsite operation. The Field Maintenance Engineer (FME) interacts with the service layer’s FME Copilot via a dedicated Mobile application to retrieve relevant fault information about the affected base station (8). The service layer FME Copilot then coordinates with the resource layer FME Copilot, which supplies the FME with natural language-based operational guidance to facilitate efficient fault resolution (9).
